doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Moms Mabley, Peg Leg Bates and learning to stop a show
summary: On two theatre dates with the Sweethearts and Moms Mabley she learned from comedians who stopped shows; closers on the bill were the biggest acts.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Somewhere around this time, it’s never dated, you were doing some package tours with both the International Sweethearts of Rhythm and Jackie “Moms” Mabley. Was that the same tour, were they on the package together with you?
I must have done two theatres with them. Jackie “Moms” Mabley, she said, she’d stop the show and say, “Follow that.”

She’d put her teeth in the glass, perform, she was a comedian, you know. She’d perform and stop the show. So, that’s how you learn how to stop a show, with performers like that. And then there was another performer, Peg Leg Bates, had one leg. He’d say, “Let me break this other leg for you.”
On that kind of package, what would the order be, the order of artists?
They would close it. ‘Cause I don’t think I could close it then. Now I could.
